## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are **scheduled batch processes** that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus of documents. They run on a fixed cadence (rather than on demand) and handle both total re-embedding and incremental updates when:

- The underlying embedding model changes (e.g., upgraded to a newer or alternative model)
- Source documents update in bulk
- The retrieval index requires a full rebuild

## Key Characteristics

### Scheduling and Scope
- Fixed-cadence execution rather than event-driven or on-demand
- Can re-embed the full document set or an incremental subset
- Allows controllable, predictable resource consumption compared to continuous embedding

### Atomic Deployment
New vectors are swapped into the retrieval index **atomically** to prevent serving mixed-model results during transition. This ensures that:
- Queries use a single, consistent embedding model at any point in time
- No stale or hybrid results leak to users during the cutover

### Operational Practices

#### Model Versioning
- Each batch must version the embedding model it uses
- Enables tracking which model produced which embeddings
- Critical for debugging and rollback decisions

#### Drift Monitoring
- Monitor **vector drift** between old embeddings and newly generated ones
- Detect whether the new model produces significantly different representations
- Identify potential quality regressions before they reach production

#### Staging and Rollback
- Stage the new index behind a **blue/green deployment** strategy
- Run validation/quality checks on the green index before promoting it
- Enable rapid rollback if the new index shows quality regression

## Related Concepts

- [[blue-green-deployment]] — The staging pattern used to safely roll out new embeddings
- [[vector-databases]] — The index target for embedding storage and retrieval
- [[retrieval-augmented-generation]] — A common use case requiring stable, versioned embeddings
